newsitem.title: MEXICO: Police bust kidnapping ring in northern Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Police bust kidnapping ring in northern Mexico.

text.p: Police in the northern Mexican state of Sonora said on Thursday they had captured five members of a kidnapping ring that had been targeting wealthy business people in several northern Mexican states.

One of those arrested, Cornelio Galindo Perez, 24, participated in the August kidnapping of a Japanese electronics executive in the northern border city of Tijuana, Sonora state Judicial Police agent Hervin Araiza said.
The band has been involved in at least six kidnappings in the northern states of Sonora, Chihuahua, Sinaloa and Baja California, Araiza said.
"This is a very well-organised kidnapping band," he said. "But the principal members of the band are others."
Araiza said five men were arrested on Tuesday after police caught them watching Luis Pericles Dravos, a former mayor and owner of a retail shop, from a car parked outside his home.
The kidnapping of the Japanese executive in Tijuana drew international attention to Mexico's kidnapping epidemic, in which wealthy business people are abducted for ransom.
In many cases, relatives don't report the incidents to police for fear that corrupt officers might be in league with the kidnappers.

Mamoru Konno, 57, president of a U.S. subsidiary of Japan's Sanyo Electric Co, was kidnapped on August 10 while attending a company picnic in Tijuana, where Sanyo has a major assembly plant. He was on his way home to San Diego, California, which is across the border from Tijuana.
Konno was freed after Sanyo paid a $2 million ransom in unmarked $100 bills, officials said.
